title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Are DataColumnSidecarsByRange response sizes properly bounded?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The handler uses a quota variable (maxRequestDataColumnSidecars = 16384) as the primary bound on response size. The quota is decremented by 1 per sidecar written. However, the initial rate-limiter validation uses rateLimitingAmount=1 (a single fixed constant represent
state_anomalies_found: CRITICAL: Initial validateRequest() charges only rateLimitingAmount=1 for the entire range request regardless of how many sidecars will actually be served. The bucket capacity is allowedDataColumnsBurst = DataColumnBatchLimitBurstFactor * DataColumnBatchLimit = 2 * 4096 = 8192. A peer's bucket starts with 8192 capacity. The initial check only subtracts 1, so the check will pass if remaining >= 1 (not >= expected_response_size). The per-sidecar charges happen AFTER writing, so they don't prevent the sidecar from being sent.

Rate limiter inconsistency: validateRequest uses remaining >= rateLimitingAmount (1) as a gate, but then up to 16384 sidecars are served with per-sidecar rateLimiter.add() calls. The gate is thus almost always open.

The quota (MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars=16384) bounds total sidecars sent in one response, but the leaky bucket with capacity 8192 (default) means after the initial burst, a second request can be sent immediately and another 8192 units are available. The effective per-peer rate is governed by the leaky bucket drain rate, not by the quota.

wantedColumns is taken directly from request.Columns without validating column index values are within [0, NumberOfColumns-1]. The storage.Get() function does validate via storageIndices.get() which returns error for index >= 128, but the handler does not pre-validate.

Quota underflow guard: 'if quota == 0 { return 0, nil }' is present in streamDataColumnBatch before the main loop, but quota -= 1 can only underflow if quota is 0 at the point of subtraction. Since the guard checks quota==0 after decrement, and the outer guard checks quota==0 before decrement, there is no underflow risk.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: The dataColumnStorage.Get() reads from the filesystem cache (pruneMu.RLock) and per-file mutex (fileMu.RLock). Cache is updated on Save() and evicted on Remove(). No inconsistency visible in read path during RPC serving.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Multiple concurrent range requests from same peer share the same leaky bucket per peer-ID. rateLimiter.validateRequest() holds RLock, rateLimiter.add() holds write Lock. Race between validateRequest check and add calls from concurrent goroutines is possible: two concurrent requests each pass validateRequest (remaining >= 1) but together consume 2*16384=32768 units. The leaky bucket will absorb these charges but won't prevent both requests from completing since the gate was already passed.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: An attacker can request 128 columns across MaxSlotsPerRequest slots to maximize response size. With validateRequest() only checking 'remaining >= 1', the gate is almost always open. The effective limit is MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars=16384 sidecars per response. With 128 columns per slot, 16384 / 128 = 128 slots. Each sidecar is a full data column (~128KB for a maximally-full blob), so a maximally large response can be 128 * 128KB = 16MB per request. The bucket capacity of 8192 and drain rate of 4096/30s means after spending 16384 units for a full response, the peer must wait ~2*30s=60s for full recovery, but since validateRequest only checks 'remaining >= 1', not 'remaining >= 16384', a peer can immediately send another request if even 1 unit has drained.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: EXPLOIT: Attacker sends DataColumnSidecarsByRangeRequest{StartSlot=current-128, Count=128, Columns=[0..127]}. validateRequest(stream, 1) passes as long as remaining >= 1 (almost always true). rangeParameters are valid. streamDataColumnBatch serves up to 128 columns * 128 slots = 16384 sidecars. After 8192 units charged by rateLimiter.add() calls, the bucket is full. However, the quota check maxRequestDataColumnSidecars==0 terminates at 16384 sidecars. So the attacker can sustain ~16384 sidecars every ~40 seconds (8192 unit capacity / 4096 units/30s drain rate). This is a significantly higher bandwidth drain than intended since validateRequest effectively gates on 1 unit instead of the actual response size.
attack_scenarios: Scenario 1 - Rate limiter bypass: Send repeated DataColumnSidecarsByRange requests each requesting all 128 columns across 128 slots. Each request passes the validateRequest gate (costs only 1 unit) but generates up to 16384 sidecar responses. Peer bucket (capacity 8192) fills up after first response via per-sidecar adds, but gate check only requires 1 unit remaining, so requests can be sent after partial bucket drain.

Scenario 2 - Concurrent exhaustion: Open multiple streams from the same peer simultaneously. Each stream independently calls validateRequest (each checks remaining >= 1 and passes). Multiple concurrent streams can generate 16384*N sidecars in parallel before the rate limiter's per-sidecar adds block further requests via bucket overflow (but overflow is handled asynchronously after write, not before).

Scenario 3 - Duplicate column indices: Columns field is not deduplicated before storage.Get(). storage.Get() iterates the indices slice including duplicates and calls storageIndices.get() for each, which returns the same column multiple times. The quota is decremented per-result, so duplicated columns count against quota, but the server writes the same column sidecar multiple times. This wastes quota and bandwidth but could also be used to cause a mismatch between what was requested and what was sent.
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: The concurrent scenario requires opening multiple streams near-simultaneously before the leaky bucket drains. The race between validateRequest (RLock) and rateLimiter.add (Lock) is timing-sensitive but achievable with persistent connection.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: This is a P2P RPC handler directly exposed to any libp2p peer. Any node that establishes a libp2p connection to the target can send DataColumnSidecarsByRange v1 requests. No authentication or authorization is required beyond connection establishment. The handler is registered in rpc.go for the RPCDataColumnSidecarsByRangeTopicV1 topic.
entry_points: libp2p P2P network - any peer can open a stream on /eth2/beacon_chain/req/data_column_sidecars_by_range/1/ssz_snappy
Initial sync service triggering DataColumnSidecarsByRange RPC calls
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Any libp2p peer (including adversarial nodes, Sybil nodes, or a single peer with multiple connections) can send maliciously crafted DataColumnSidecarsByRange requests. The peer just needs to be connected to the victim node.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The intended invariant is: 'Total sidecars sent per request <= MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars AND rate per peer is bounded by leaky bucket'. The quota invariant (MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars) holds correctly. However, the rate-limiting invariant is weakened because the initial gate check uses a cost of 1 instead of the expected response size, while the per-sidecar charges happen post-write. The quota correctly stops the response at 16384 sidecars. The rate limiter's per-sidecar charges will eventually fill the bucket, but the gate check on the NEXT request still only requires 1 unit remaining.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars quota (16384) bounding total sidecars per response; leaky bucket rate limiter per peer
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: INSUFFICIENT for rate limiting. The quota correctly bounds per-response size. However, the rate limiter's initial gate check uses rateLimitingAmount=1 (fixed constant) rather than checking against the expected number of sidecars to be served. The comment 'We count a single request as a single rate limiting amount, regardless of the number of columns requested' documents this as intentional, but it means the gate is nearly always open. The actual per-sidecar charges will fill the bucket eventually, but only AFTER serving the response. The per-sidecar charges are correctly charged post-write, but the gate on the next request checks remaining >= 1, allowing a new request as soon as 1 unit has drained.
edge_cases: Empty Columns field (len=0): wantedColumns = make([]uint64, 0), storage.Get(blockRoot, []) iterates no indices and returns nil/empty, so no sidecars are served. This is safe.

Columns with out-of-range indices (>= 128): storage.Get calls storageIndices.get() which returns error for index >= 128. The handler does not pre-validate, so the error propagates as a server error response. This is not a security issue but could be used for denial-of-service (forcing error path).

Duplicate column indices in Columns: storageIndices.get() returns the column for each duplicate index. verifiedRODataColumns will contain duplicate entries. Each duplicate decrements quota. The same sidecar is written multiple times to the stream, potentially confusing the requester, but quota prevents unbounded response.
count=1 with startSlot=current: single slot, single sidecar per column. Minimal valid request.
Quota uint64 starting at 16384: streamDataColumnBatch correctly returns 0 when quota reaches 0. No underflow possible since guard checks quota==0 before decrement.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The rate limiting architecture has a significant design flaw: the initial gate check (validateRequest) charges only 1 unit for any DataColumnSidecarsByRange request regardless of how many columns * slots are requested, while per-sidecar charges occur post-write. This means the gate check is nearly always satisfied (only fails if bucket is truly at 0), allowing an attacker to continuously trigger maximum-size responses (up to 16384 sidecars = ~2GB per request if columns are maximally full) limited only by the per-sidecar bucket charges. The comment in the code acknowledges this is intentional ('We count a single request as a single rate limiting amount') but the consequence is that the rate limiter gate provides minimal protection against resource exhaustion. Combined with the duplicate column index issue and multi-stream concurrent exploitation, this constitutes an exploitable resource exhaustion vulnerability.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: 1) The validateRequest call should estimate expected response size (min(Count * len(Columns), MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars)) and validate against this. 2) Deduplicate Columns before processing to prevent duplicate sidecar serving. 3) Validate column indices are in [0, NumberOfColumns-1] before storage lookup.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Is data_column_serve_range correctly enforced?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: dataColumnsRPCMinValidSlot computes the minimum slot that may be served in a DataColumnSidecarsByRange or DataColumnSidecarsByRoot request. The function uses two config-time constants (MinEpochsForDataColumnSidecarsRequest=4096, FuluForkEpoch) and the runtime currentSlot to determine the sliding window floor. The core logic branch guards an epoch subtraction with 'currEpoch > minReqEpochs' before computing 'currEpoch - minReqEpochs', protecting against uint64 underflow. The function returns Slot(math.MaxUint64) pre-Fulu to ensure no data is served before Fulu activation.
state_anomalies_found: Pre-Fulu guard: When FuluEnabled() returns false (FuluForkEpoch == math.MaxUint64), dataColumnsRPCMinValidSlot returns math.MaxUint64. In validateDataColumnsByRange, the check 'if endSlot < minStartSlot' would compare endSlot against math.MaxUint64. Since endSlot is bounded by currentSlot (which is a real slot value much less than MaxUint64), endSlot < MaxUint64 is always true, causing validateDataColumnsByRange to return nil,nil (empty response). This is the intended behavior - no data columns exist pre-Fulu. However, this silent nil return (rather than an error) does NOT penalize the requesting peer even though requesting data columns before Fulu activation is clearly invalid.

FuluEnabled() definition: 'return BeaconConfig().FuluForkEpoch < math.MaxUint64'. This means if FuluForkEpoch is set to any value < MaxUint64, Fulu is 'enabled'. The function does NOT check if the current epoch has reached FuluForkEpoch. So FuluEnabled() can return true while currEpoch < FuluForkEpoch.

Epoch underflow guard analysis: The condition 'currEpoch > minReqEpochs && currEpoch-minReqEpochs > minStartEpoch' uses short-circuit evaluation. The first part (currEpoch > minReqEpochs) guards the subtraction. primitives.Epoch is uint64, so if currEpoch <= minReqEpochs, the subtraction is skipped. This guard is correct.

minStartEpoch may be 0 if FuluForkEpoch=0 and currEpoch <= minReqEpochs. EpochStart(0) = Slot(0). This would set minStartSlot=0, meaning the server would serve columns from slot 0 onward. This is only possible if FuluForkEpoch is configured to 0.

EpochStart overflow: EpochStart calls SlotsPerEpoch.SafeMul(uint64(epoch)). With SlotsPerEpoch=32 and epoch=minStartEpoch, overflow requires epoch > MaxUint64/32 ~ 5.76e17. Since minStartEpoch is clamped by FuluForkEpoch and currEpoch (both uint64 < MaxUint64/32 in practice), no overflow occurs in realistic configurations.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: dataColumnsRPCMinValidSlot reads only from BeaconConfig() which is a global immutable config (set at startup). No cache state is involved. The result is deterministic for a given currentSlot and configuration. No TOCTOU risk.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: No shared mutable state is accessed. BeaconConfig() returns an immutable pointer. params.FuluEnabled() reads a single config value. No concurrent access issues.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: The primary attack vector is requesting data columns from before the Fulu fork epoch (when FuluEnabled returns true but current epoch < FuluForkEpoch). In this case, minStartEpoch = FuluForkEpoch (not yet reached), so minStartSlot = EpochStart(FuluForkEpoch) which is in the future. Any request with endSlot < minStartSlot returns nil,nil immediately - this is a no-op. The attacker cannot cause incorrect data to be served; at worst they receive an empty response. The integer underflow scenario is fully guarded by the 'currEpoch > minReqEpochs' check.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: No counterexample found for incorrect data being served or memory safety violations. The silent empty response (nil, nil) for pre-Fulu requests is a behavioral issue (no peer penalization) but not a data integrity vulnerability.
attack_scenarios: Scenario 1 - Pre-Fulu empty response without peer penalty: Attacker sends DataColumnSidecarsByRange with any slot range when FuluEnabled()=true but current epoch < FuluForkEpoch. dataColumnsRPCMinValidSlot returns EpochStart(FuluForkEpoch) which is a future slot. endSlot < minStartSlot, so validateDataColumnsByRange returns nil,nil. The caller sees rangeParameters==nil and returns nil without writing an error response or penalizing the peer. This allows an attacker to repeatedly probe for data columns without any peer score penalty, consuming server processing time for validation.

Scenario 2 - Boundary epoch arithmetic: When currEpoch == minReqEpochs exactly, the condition 'currEpoch > minReqEpochs' is false (not >=), so minStartEpoch stays at FuluForkEpoch. This means for exactly minReqEpochs epochs after Fulu, the minimum serve epoch is FuluForkEpoch rather than currEpoch - minReqEpochs. This is correct per spec: serve the full data retention window from the fork epoch.

Scenario 3 - startSlot clamping: If attacker sends startSlot=0, count=MaxUint64 overflow check catches startSlot.SafeAdd(count-1) overflow. If count=1, startSlot=0, endSlot=0. endSlot < minStartSlot (minStartSlot >= EpochStart(FuluForkEpoch) > 0), returns nil,nil. No data served, no penalty.
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: No timing dependency. dataColumnsRPCMinValidSlot is a pure deterministic function of currentSlot and config.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: dataColumnsRPCMinValidSlot is called from two P2P RPC handlers: validateDataColumnsByRange (in DataColumnSidecarsByRangeRPCHandler) and dataColumnSidecarByRootRPCHandler. Both handlers are directly accessible from any libp2p peer. The function itself only reads config values and does not serve data directly; it is a pure computation function. The vulnerability is in how its return value is used by the calling handlers.
entry_points: libp2p P2P - DataColumnSidecarsByRange RPC handler calls validateDataColumnsByRange which calls dataColumnsRPCMinValidSlot
libp2p P2P - DataColumnSidecarsByRoot RPC handler calls dataColumnsRPCMinValidSlot directly
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Any connected peer can trigger execution of this function. The function's output is used to gate data serving, and a misconfiguration of FuluForkEpoch could cause incorrect behavior, but in standard configurations the function is correct.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The core invariant is: 'No data columns are served for slots before max(FuluForkEpochStart, currentEpoch - MinEpochsForDataColumnSidecarsRequest)'. The integer underflow guard (currEpoch > minReqEpochs) correctly protects the subtraction. The pre-Fulu guard (FuluEnabled() returning MaxUint64) correctly returns MaxUint64 to ensure no columns are served. The EpochStart computation uses SafeMul to prevent overflow. The invariant holds for all standard configurations.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: 1) FuluEnabled() check returning MaxUint64 for pre-Fulu configurations; 2) underflow guard 'currEpoch > minReqEpochs'; 3) SafeMul overflow protection in EpochStart; 4) endSlot < minStartSlot early return in validateDataColumnsByRange; 5) startSlot = max(startSlot, minStartSlot) clamping
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: SUFFICIENT for data integrity. The serve range is correctly bounded: no pre-fork columns are served, and no columns older than MinEpochsForDataColumnSidecarsRequest are served (when epoch is sufficiently advanced). The only gap is that requests for pre-Fulu data return nil,nil (empty, no error) rather than an explicit error response, which means peers are not penalized for invalid requests. This is a minor behavioral issue, not a data integrity vulnerability.
edge_cases: FuluForkEpoch=0: FuluEnabled() returns true (0 < MaxUint64). minStartEpoch=0, currEpoch >= 0. If currEpoch > minReqEpochs=4096, minStartEpoch slides. EpochStart(0)=Slot(0). This is an extreme misconfiguration not used in production.
currEpoch == minReqEpochs: condition is false (not >=), minStartEpoch stays at FuluForkEpoch. Correct per spec.

FuluEnabled() returns true but currentEpoch < FuluForkEpoch: minStartEpoch = FuluForkEpoch (future), minStartSlot is in the future, all requests return nil,nil. Peer is not penalized. This allows repeated probing without penalty.

MaxUint64 slot value: The pre-Fulu path returns MaxUint64. In validateDataColumnsByRange, endSlot is computed via SafeAdd(count-1) and then clamped to min(endSlot, currentSlot). currentSlot << MaxUint64. So endSlot < MaxUint64 always when Fulu is disabled.

SafeAdd overflow in EpochStart: EpochStart calls SlotsPerEpoch.SafeMul(epoch). With SlotsPerEpoch=32, overflow only at epoch > 5.76e17. FuluForkEpoch on mainnet is MaxUint64, but dataColumnsRPCMinValidSlot only calls EpochStart when FuluEnabled() is true, meaning FuluForkEpoch < MaxUint64. The resulting EpochStart(FuluForkEpoch) could theoretically overflow if FuluForkEpoch > 5.76e17, but this would be caught by the SafeMul error return.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The serve range logic in dataColumnsRPCMinValidSlot is correct and all guards are sufficient. The only identified issue is that invalid pre-Fulu requests return nil,nil (empty response with no peer penalty) rather than an explicit rejection. This is a non-penalizing silent response rather than an exploitable vulnerability: the attacker cannot obtain incorrect data, cannot cause crashes, and cannot bypass the data retention window. The rate limiter still charges the initial validateRequest cost (1 unit) for the by-range handler. The issue is at most a minor behavioral gap in peer scoring, which does not meet the bar for bug bounty eligibility as a security vulnerability.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Consider returning an explicit error response (p2ptypes.ErrInvalidRequest) for data column requests when FuluEnabled() is true but the current epoch has not yet reached FuluForkEpoch, so that peers making invalid requests are penalized via downscorePeer(). This improves peer scoring accuracy but is not a security-critical fix.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRoot reject requests exceeding MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: validateDataColumnsByRootRequest sums uint64(len(id.Columns)) for each DataColumnsByRootIdentifier in the request and rejects if total > MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars (16384). The SSZ deserialization constrains: (a) the list length to MaxRequestBlocksDeneb=128 identifiers via the types.DataColumnsByRootIdentifiers.UnmarshalSSZ check, and (b) each identifier's Columns list to 128 entries via DivideInt2(len(buf), 8, 128) in the proto SSZ. The total check thus operates over at most 128*128=16384 columns. The serving loop then iterates over requestedColumnIdents (the ORIGINAL list), not the deduplicated map, creating a critical behavioral gap.
state_anomalies_found: CRITICAL: The deduplication map requestedColumnsByRoot is built but used ONLY for logging. The serving loop 'for _, ident := range requestedColumnIdents' iterates over the original list including duplicate BlockRoots. An attacker can send 128 identifiers each referencing the same BlockRoot with 128 columns each (total=16384, passes validation). The server then calls dataColumnStorage.Get(root, columns) 128 separate times for the same root, multiplying disk I/O by 128x.

Integer overflow in total accumulation: total starts at uint64(0) and accumulates uint64(len(id.Columns)). Maximum: 128 identifiers * 128 columns = 16384, far below uint64 max (~1.8e19). No overflow possible given SSZ constraints.

Empty Columns list: An identifier with len(id.Columns)=0 contributes 0 to total and passes validation. The serving loop then calls storage.Get(root, []) for an empty columns slice, which returns an empty result. The for-range loop over columns (len=0) increments count by 0. rateLimiter.add(stream, 0) is a no-op. This is harmless.

Rate limiter: The by-root handler does NOT call s.rateLimiter.validateRequest() before processing, unlike the by-range handler which does. The by-root handler only calls rateLimiter.add(stream, int64(len(columns))) after processing each identifier. There is no upfront budget check.

Throttle mechanism interaction with duplicates: batchSize=4096 (default DataColumnBatchLimit). The ticker is created if len(requestedColumnIdents) > batchSize. With 128 identifiers and up to 16384 total columns, the count variable tracks total columns processed. count%batchSize==0 triggers <-ticker.C (1 second sleep). Duplicate roots contribute to count, so duplicate-heavy requests may trigger MORE throttle sleeps than expected.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: dataColumnStorage.Get() involves disk I/O and in-memory index lookups. For each BlockRoot, the storage layer performs a filesystem read. Calling Get(sameRoot, columns) 128 times for the same root means 128 separate disk reads for the same data. There is no deduplication at the storage layer for repeated requests of the same root.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: The per-root duplicate attack causes 128 sequential Get() calls for the same root within a single goroutine. No concurrent access issue specific to this vulnerability. However, if multiple peers simultaneously exploit this (each sending 128-duplicate requests), the disk I/O multiplier becomes 128*N for N concurrent peers.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: An attacker constructs a DataColumnSidecarsByRoot request containing 128 DataColumnsByRootIdentifier entries all with the same BlockRoot and each with 128 columns (total=16384, exactly at the limit). validateDataColumnsByRootRequest passes because total==16384 == MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars (not >). The serving loop iterates 128 times over the same root, calling storage.Get(sameRoot, [0..127]) 128 times. Each call reads the same set of up to 128 data column sidecars from disk. The total disk reads are multiplied by 128x. Additionally, each identifier's 128 sidecars (if present) are written to the stream, potentially sending up to 128*128=16384 sidecars all for the same block root.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: EXPLOIT - Disk I/O amplification and duplicate sidecar serving: Craft request with 128 identical DataColumnsByRootIdentifier{BlockRoot=<canonical_root>, Columns=[0,1,...,127]}. Total columns=16384, passes validateDataColumnsByRootRequest (16384 is NOT > 16384). Server iterates 128 times, calling storage.Get(same_root, [0..127]) each time. Each call returns up to 128 sidecars (if stored). Total sidecars served: up to 128*128=16384 (quota is the only limit, but there is no global quota in the by-root handler unlike by-range). All 16384 sidecars are for the same block root, sent to the attacker. Disk I/O amplification: 128x reads of the same block's columns. The attacker receives 16384 duplicate sidecars for a single block root.
attack_scenarios: Scenario 1 - Disk I/O amplification DoS: Send 128 identifiers all referencing the same BlockRoot with all 128 columns. Server performs 128 Get() calls (each a disk read) for the same root instead of 1. For popular/hot roots, even if caching helps, this still multiplies processing work by 128x. For cold roots (pruned from memory), this triggers 128 disk seeks for the same data.

Scenario 2 - Bandwidth amplification: The same 16384 sidecars (128 sets of 128 columns per root) are all written to the stream. Total bandwidth usage is 128x what should have been served for a single root. The attacker receives 128 copies of each column for the same block.

Scenario 3 - Rate limiter exhaustion: rateLimiter.add(stream, int64(len(columns))) is called 128 times with len(columns)=128, totaling 16384 units charged to the rate limiter. This depletes the peer's rate limiter bucket just as much as a legitimate full request. However, the work done by the server is 128x more than a single-root full request.

Scenario 4 - total==MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars boundary: total=16384 is NOT > 16384, so the validation check 'if total > MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars' does NOT reject this. The off-by-one means a request with exactly MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars columns via a single identifier OR via 128 duplicate identifiers both pass equally. The intent may have been to allow exactly MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars columns, but duplicates defeat this.
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: No timing required. The exploit is deterministic: construct the malicious request once and send it. The 128x amplification is guaranteed by the code path.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The DataColumnSidecarsByRoot RPC handler is directly accessible from any libp2p peer that is connected to the target node. It is registered in rpc.go for RPCDataColumnSidecarsByRootTopicV1. No authentication is required. The handler processes the request synchronously in a goroutine per stream, so each connection can have multiple concurrent streams.
entry_points: libp2p P2P network - any peer can open a stream on /eth2/beacon_chain/req/data_column_sidecars_by_root/1/ssz_snappy
Light clients or data availability sampling clients requesting specific column sidecars by root
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Any connected peer can send a crafted DataColumnSidecarsByRoot request. The SSZ deserialization enforces the 128-identifier list limit and 128-columns-per-identifier limit, but these limits do not prevent the duplicate-root attack which achieves 128x I/O amplification within those limits.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The intended invariant is: 'Total columns requested <= MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars AND each unique block root is fetched at most once per request'. The first part (total <= MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars) is enforced by validateDataColumnsByRootRequest. The second part is NOT enforced. The deduplication map requestedColumnsByRoot is built but is only used for logging - the serving loop uses the original requestedColumnIdents list. This means the invariant 'each unique root fetched at most once' is violated whenever duplicate BlockRoots appear.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: validateDataColumnsByRootRequest (total column count check); SSZ deserialization (128 identifier limit, 128 column per identifier limit); rate limiter add per identifier
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: INSUFFICIENT. The total column count guard correctly prevents requesting more than MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars columns. However, it does not prevent the same root from being specified multiple times with identical or different column sets. The deduplication map that WAS built in the handler (requestedColumnsByRoot) would have been sufficient to prevent this if the serving loop used it instead of the original list - but it does not. The rate limiter correctly charges per column processed but does not prevent 128x disk I/O amplification since the work happens before the rate limiting blocks future requests.
edge_cases: Identical columns across duplicate roots: root A with columns [0..127] repeated 128 times. Total=16384, passes. Server reads same data 128 times, writes same 128 sidecars 128 times (16384 total writes). No quota mechanism in by-root handler to stop at a threshold unlike by-range handler.

Mixed unique and duplicate roots: 64 unique roots with columns [0..127] + 64 duplicate entries for root X with columns [0..127]. Total=128*128=16384, passes. Server fetches 64 unique roots once each + root X 64 more times. I/O amplification is partial (64x for root X).
Empty columns in one identifier: 127 identifiers with 128 columns + 1 identifier with 0 columns. Total=16256 < 16384, passes. Empty-column identifier triggers Get(root, []) = empty result. Harmless.

Missing rate limit validateRequest call: Unlike by-range handler, by-root handler does NOT call s.rateLimiter.validateRequest() before starting work. Validation only rejects structurally invalid requests. There is no upfront budget check, meaning a peer with an empty rate limiter bucket can still trigger full processing.

No quota in by-root handler: Unlike streamDataColumnBatch in the by-range handler which has a quota counter (maxRequestDataColumnSidecars decremented per sidecar), the by-root handler has no equivalent quota. If 128 duplicate identifiers each with 128 columns result in 128*128=16384 sidecar writes, there is no early exit. All 16384 writes proceed.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Two distinct exploitable issues exist: (1) Duplicate BlockRoot amplification: An attacker sends 128 identifiers all referencing the same BlockRoot, passing the validateDataColumnsByRootRequest check (total=16384 which is NOT > 16384). The deduplication map built in the handler is not used for serving, so the storage is queried 128 times for the same root. This achieves 128x disk I/O amplification and 128x bandwidth amplification (the same sidecar set is sent 128 times). (2) Missing upfront rate limit validateRequest call: Unlike the by-range handler, the by-root handler does not call rateLimiter.validateRequest() before processing, meaning a peer with a depleted bucket still triggers full processing before the post-hoc add() charges would eventually block future requests. Together these constitute an exploitable Denial of Service vulnerability reachable from any connected P2P peer.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: 1) Use the already-constructed requestedColumnsByRoot deduplication map for the serving loop instead of iterating over the original requestedColumnIdents list. This eliminates duplicate root fetches while preserving union of requested columns. 2) Add s.rateLimiter.validateRequest(stream, int64(total)) upfront where total is the validated column count. 3) Consider adding a per-response quota similar to the by-range handler to bound total sidecars written.
